chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Ajlan, Abu Salih, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) dictated:

"In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate." This is what so-and-so ibn so-and-so gave in charity while he was alive and sound of body, in his house which is among the Banu so-and-so, with its boundaries, as a charity that is not to be sold nor given away, until Allah inherits it, who inherits the heavens and the earth. And he has made this charity of his reside with so-and-so and his descendants. So when they have perished, it is for the needy among the Muslims.

key_terms.لاَ تُبَاعُ وَ لاَ تُوهَبُ: not to be sold nor given away (inalienable)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal formula for establishing a permanent charitable endowment (sadaqah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the jurisprudential framework for *waqf* (endowment) by detailing the specific verbal formula required for validity. It highlights the Shia legal principle of inalienability (*la tuba'u wa la tuhabbu*), ensuring the asset remains dedicated to its charitable purpose while providing for the donor's lineage before reverting to the general Muslim community. This text serves as a foundational model for Islamic charitable trusts, emphasizing the permanence of the endowed property.
